For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.

title: Ground state and thermal phase diagrams of the magnetized spin-$1/2$ XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice
summary: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $\Psi$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$\Psi$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
summary: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $\epsilon_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $\alpha^2(36\pi^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192\pi^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $\alpha = (4/9\pi)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.

title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
summary: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

title: Spin Hamiltonian, magnetic anisotropy and excitation spectrum in altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe from first principles
summary: The hexagonal altermagnet $\alpha$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $\alpha$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $\Gamma$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $\alpha$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.

title: Universal spectrum of weakly coupled quantum critical Ising chains
summary: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $\psi$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrm{\psi}/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

title: Contribution to the GdTe$_3$ magnetic phase diagram from electronic transport measurements
summary: Magnetic phase diagrams of the three antiferromagnetic (AFM) transitions of GdTe$_3$ that occur at zero magnetic field at $T_{N1}=12$ K, $T_{N2}=10.5$ K and $T_1=7$ K are investigated by means of resistance measurements in a magnetic field oriented along the three crystallographic directions. With the magnetic field applied in the basal plane we found re-entrance of an intermediate phase which may be a result of the coupling between the $T_{N2}$ AFM and the charge density wave with possibly a ferroaxial order. A spin flop transition is also observed at a temperature that presumably converges towards a triple point in vicinity of 2.5-3.0 T and $T$ between $T_1$ and $T_{N2}$. Our results help complete a complex phase diagram of GdTe$_3$ and advance a method for investigating magnetic ordering via transport measurements -- a technique applicable to many other compounds.

title: Space-Time Point Defects as Probes of Criticality: Application to the Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg Transition
summary: At criticality, a local field acting at a single point in Euclidean space-time is irrelevant and induces a modulation in space and time that decays with twice its scaling dimension. This turns two-point correlation functions into one-point measurements: one operator insertion enters the Boltzmann weight, the other is measured. For the local magnetization the relation is exact at any source strength. Implemented in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, the approach yields the static spin susceptibility and imaginary-time-displaced correlations with unprecedented precision. We apply it to the Dirac-semimetal to antiferromagnetic-Mott-insulator transition of the half-filled $\pi$-flux Hubbard model. This lattice model provides a regularization of the $N_f=2$ Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg universality class. A finite-size scaling analysis estimates the critical exponents as $ \nu=1.10(3)$ and $\eta_\phi=1.09(4)$, close to field-theory predictions of $\eta_\phi\simeq1$. Since $\eta_\phi>1$, the equal-time structure factor at criticality does not diverge with the system size. Hence, the equal-time structure factor at the ordering wave vector is dominated by background contributions and cannot be used for extracting critical exponents. Consistently, the spin dynamics at the transition is strongly incoherent and the quantum Fisher information remains bounded.

title: Zone-folded Goldstone mode of the field-induced spin supersolid in the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet
summary: The field-induced spin supersolid of the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet with single-ion and exchange anisotropy has so far been characterized only by static observables, among them a two-peak transverse structure factor. We compute its dynamic spin structure factors, and those of the neighboring phases, by stochastic analytic continuation of stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo data on a $16\times16$ lattice at inverse temperature $\beta=32$, at one field in each of the supersolid, the $m_z=1/2$ Ising plateau and the canted $XY$ phase. The supersolid has a single Goldstone mode, which the checkerboard folds onto both the ordering wave vector $\mathbf{Q}=(\pi,\pi)$ and $\mathbf{q}=(0,0)$, so that it appears in both spin channels at both points with one velocity $v=1.36\pm0.01$. The canted phase shows half of this pattern and the plateau none, the latter carrying instead a gapped magnon band and a two-magnon longitudinal continuum. Exactly at $\mathbf{Q}$ and $(0,0)$ the finite-lattice spectra are governed by a rotor tower of the condensate in the transverse channel and an Ising doublet of the checkerboard in the longitudinal one, both present at $\mathbf{Q}$ in the supersolid. Three parameter-free comparisons with the stiffness and the uniform susceptibility of the same runs, for the velocity, the sound-mode weight and the thermal decay of the rotor tower, tie the continued spectra to raw Monte Carlo observables. The folded Goldstone mode is the dynamical fingerprint of the supersolid.

title: Local Thermodynamic Reconstruction of Impurity Entropy
summary: Resolving the thermodynamic entropy associated with a local impurity in a spatially extended interacting quantum bath remains a numerical challenge. We develop a Local-Maxwell approach that reconstructs the impurity entropy from local observables in worldline quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. By integrating their temperature responses along the impurity coupling, the method avoids separate estimates of extensive entropies. For nonnegative worldline expansions with bounded local couplings, we establish bath-size independent bounds on all factorial moments of the impurity vertex count. For even vertex counts, the Maxwell estimator variance remains bounded as the coupling approaches zero. The transverse-field Ising benchmark reproduces exact free fermion results, while an interacting XXZ chain demonstrates up to several hundredfold improvement in statistical efficiency over conventional extensive thermodynamic integration. In a three-channel XXZ impurity junction, we reveal entropy recovery upon cooling and a nonmonotonic coupling dependence of the finite-temperature entropy contrast. These results establish local thermodynamic reconstruction as an efficient approach to impurity entropy in interacting quantum baths.

title: Investigating competing order in the Kanamori-Hubbard model with the multiorbital multichannel fluctuating field theory
summary: The multichannel fluctuating field (MCFF) approach treats selected collective fluctuations in interacting quantum lattice models nonperturbatively, but has so far been applied only to single-band systems. Here, we extend MCFF theory to multiorbital systems, accounting for the orbital structure of charge and spin instabilities. We apply it to the half-filled two-orbital Kanamori-Hubbard model with repulsive intra-orbital interaction $U$, and both positive and negative Hund's coupling $J$, addressing the competing orders and their interplay. The ability to selectively retain individual fluctuation channels and control their interplay allows us to disentangle their respective contributions and identify the mechanisms underlying competing instabilities. The model features a simple competition between charge density wave and antiferromagnetic fluctuations in the vicinity of $J=U$, and a more intricate competition between antiferromagnetic, orbital, and spin-orbital fluctuations near $J=0$, where the model acquires a higher SU(4) symmetry. The proposed multiorbital extension thus provides a computationally inexpensive and efficient framework for exploring how orbital and spin character shape competing collective fluctuations.

title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
summary: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.

title: Band-Selective Coupling to Charge Density Wave Fluctuations in Kagome Superconductors AV3Sb5
summary: The kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) host multiband superconductivity (SC) within an unconventional charge density wave (CDW) parent phase, yet the relationship between the two remains unresolved. Through time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments on CsV3Sb5 and KV3Sb5, we observe coherent band oscillations driven by coupling to a low-energy CDW amplitude mode at 3.1 THz. We find this coupling to be highly band-selective, differing by a factor of over 2 even between bands with dominant V-3d character. We reproduce these results with frozen-phonon density functional theory calculations, offering insight towards the relation between differing Fermi surface characters and our observed band selectivity. Furthermore, we observe differences in coupling channels between KV3Sb5 and CsV3Sb5. These results establish CDW amplitude mode fluctuations as a band-selective low-energy coupling channel that intimately contributes to the interplay between CDW and SC in the AV3Sb5 compounds.

title: Tunneling signatures of the Lifshitz transition in a superconducting vortex
summary: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\sim\Delta^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.

title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
summary: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

title: Majorana flat bands from mirror-particle-hole antisymmetry
summary: Majorana flat bands, zero modes across the whole edge Brillouin zone, usually rest on chiral symmetry. We show that a fully gapped class-D superconductor can host such a flat band without chiral symmetry or time reversal, provided its superconducting gap is odd under a mirror and translation along the edge is preserved. Combined with particle--hole conjugation, the mirror forms an antiunitary antisymmetry that squares to $+1$ and preserves the momentum along the edge, so it fixes the Kitaev index of every slice of fixed edge momentum. In a gapped bulk, this slice index cannot change with the edge momentum, and the edge zero modes form a band across the whole edge Brillouin zone. We construct a four-band model with exactly these symmetries, a helical $p$-wave superconductor with Rashba coupling in an in-plane exchange field, from which no term can be removed without restoring an additional symmetry. On the mirror lines, its two mirror sectors are exact Kitaev chains. This yields a closed-form phase diagram. Besides the flat band, the model hosts a phase with two Majoranas at each end of a wire, although its class-D index is trivial, and a second-order phase with Majorana corner modes. The spectral localizer detects all these indices in real space, directly on finite-size samples as relevant for experiments. On open rectangular flakes of two widths, it reproduces the phase diagram even though translational symmetry is broken. In the nodal regions, its reading depends on the flake size, so they are left unread. The readings persist under disorder several times the bulk gap. Without translation along the edge, the symmetries protect no more than Majorana parities, and we quantify the signatures that remain specific to the antisymmetry. A minimal model of magnetic adatoms on a triplet superconductor realizes the flat-band and second-order phases.

title: Magnetoelectric response to a N\'eel domain wall in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films: Spontaneous currents, vortex pinning, and vortex-antivortex nucleation
summary: We study the superconducting response induced by a N\'eel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single N\'eel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the N\'eel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by N\'eel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.

title: Topological Anderson Superconductor in Landau Levels
summary: There is much interest in two-dimensional superconductors with odd integer values of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Chern number $C_{\rm BdG}$, often termed topological superconductors, as these are predicted to harbor Majorana zero modes. Because a magnetic field produces Landau levels (LL) with nonzero Chern numbers, it is natural to ask if a conventional two-dimensional superconductor of spinful fermions with Rashba spin-orbit coupling can be driven topological by application of a magnetic field. Self-consistent solutions of the BdG equations for an on-site attractive interaction produce a phase diagram consisting almost everywhere of superconducting states with even integer values of $C_{\rm BdG}$, transitioning from one value to another as parameters such as the chemical potential are varied. We predict that introducing Anderson-type on-site disorder, which broadens as well as mixes LLs, produces, in the transition region, states wherein topological superconductivity percolates. This topological Anderson superconducting state provides another example where disorder can produce topologically nontrivial states.

title: Current-Dependent Meta-GGA and Local Hybrid Functionals for Relativistic NMR Shifts
summary: NMR chemical shifts are key for the characterization of novel compounds. Especially for molecules with heavy elements, the experimental data is often corroborated with computational studies in density functional theory (DFT). However, modern meta-generalized gradient approximations (meta-GGAs) and local hybrid functionals are not widely supported in relativistic calculations with quantum chemistry program suites. So far, their current-dependent generalization in the spirit of Dobson, Becke, and Tao was not presented at all. This generalization ensures gauge invariance and does not introduce artifacts--unlike the more popular field-dependent generalization of the kinetic-energy density. In non-relativistic and scalar-relativistic calculations, the first was shown to be superior but the current density only arises due to the magnetic field perturbation. In contrast, spin--orbit coupling also induces current densities in the preceding ground-state calculation and the DFT framework needs to be generalized to a current density functional theory (CDFT) for consistency with the current-dependent response equations. Herein, we present the two-component relativistic generalization of the current-dependent kinetic-energy density of a Kramers-restricted Kohn--Sham reference for meta-GGAs and local hybrid functionals in NMR calculations. The extension is invariant under a position-dependent phase and a position-dependent spin rotation of the spinors, or a local U(1)$\times$SU(2) transformation. Relativistic effects are considered with exact two-component theory using a superposition of atomic potentials to include the two-electron picture-change correction (SAP-X2C).

title: Sum rules for the relativistic and retarded Bethe approximation in electron-neutral-atom collisions
summary: For high partial waves the reactance matrix for electron-atom collisions may be replaced by the Bethe approximation, and for optically allowed transitions the slowly convergent sum over partial waves can then be performed exactly by means of the sum rules of Burgess. For neutral targets the Bethe integrals and the sum rules take a particularly simple form in terms of Legendre functions of the second kind of a single argument $\chi=(k^2+k'^2)/2kk'$. We show that this structure survives in a fully relativistic description. For a projectile described by free Dirac waves interacting through the retarded M{\o}ller interaction, the Bethe integrals of every multipole order are obtained from the static ones by the replacement $\chi\to\chi_q=(k^2+k'^2-q^2)/2kk'$, where $q$ is the energy transfer divided by $c$. For dipole transitions we give closed-form sum rules over all partial waves above any $l_0\ge2$ for the Coulomb (charge-density) interaction, for the magnetic dipole interaction and for the long-range transverse electric interaction, including its interference with the Coulomb term. In each case the sum reduces to a quadratic form in $Q_{l_0-1}(\chi_q)$ and $Q_{l_0}(\chi_q)$ with coefficients rational in $l_0$. As the impact energy increases $\chi_q\to1$ and the partial-wave sums converge ever more slowly, so that the sum rules become most useful precisely in the relativistic regime.

title: OMNI-P3x universal neural network potential for large-scale computational photochemistry workflows
summary: Computational photochemistry supports the design and understanding of new materials. However, the high cost of excited-state quantum-mechanical (QM) calculations makes screening large molecular libraries prohibitively expensive. To address this limitation, we introduce OMNI-P3x, a universal machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) for singlet ground- and excited-state simulations of neutral and charged organic molecules. Trained on both ground- and excited-state conformations, it performs complete computational photochemistry workflows with accuracy approaching TD-DFT. We demonstrate its practical applicability by screening a combinatorial library of 234,375 flavylium derivatives, where the pretrained model performs ground-state geometry optimization and predicts absorption properties without additional QM calculations. Following fine-tuning, we further screen 162,960 xanthene-based dyes, identifying new candidates for red, near-infrared and short-wavelength infrared emission. Furthermore, state-dependent neural charges, learned without reference atomic charges, provide an interpretable picture of intramolecular charge redistribution upon excitation.

title: Nonemissive Intermediates: Photon-Yield Limits and Timing Advantages for Optogenetic Light
summary: Maximizing photon yield need not minimize the excitation required for a brief optogenetic stimulus. We consider a reversible luminescent source in which a mechanically prepared excitation can reach the emitter directly or through one nonemissive intermediate. Dividing the mechanically prepared photon yield by the yield from direct optical excitation of the emitter gives the probability of successful arrival. When intermediate loss is positive, the same two yields predict the mean photoluminescence emission time given independently calibrated terminal rates and thermal weights. A separate optical decay trace can test this prediction. For a fixed budget of squared transfer couplings and allocation-independent terminal losses, we prove that either direct transfer or a pure relay attains the maximum total yield. Above a sharp threshold in the intermediate loss rate, direct transfer is globally optimal. In a spectrally weighted model of the light-gated channel Chrimson, a fixed relay in this regime emits 5.21% fewer photons per prepared excitation than direct transfer. Its earlier emission produces the same mean conductance over 20 ms with 16.54% less effective preparation and leaves lower residual conductance at 50 ms. Weak-drive response kernels show how early photons contribute to activation while leaving time for closure. Sustained stimulation can favor direct transfer again. Replaying calibrated emission waveforms with a common spectrum in voltage-clamped cells would test which source meets both conductance targets with fewer prepared excitations.

title: Perturbation of CO A1{\Pi} by a3{\Pi} should have been undetectable: detection, mechanism, and surprises
summary: A direct perturbation between the $a^3\Pi$ and $A^1\Pi$ vibrational levels of two electronic states that belong to the same electronic configuration of the carbon monoxide molecule should be unobservably weak because the vibrational overlap integral $\langle a^3\Pi,v' \mid A^1\Pi,v'' \rangle$ for their near-degenerate levels is extremely small. Yet level-shift and transition-intensity signatures of the $a^3\Pi(v = 13) \sim A^1\Pi(v = 2)$ perturbation are unmistakably present in the $^{13}\mathrm{C}^{18}\mathrm{O}$ isotopologue. A detailed study of, among others, the $A^1\Pi$ - $X^1\Sigma^+(2, 0)$, $B^1\Sigma^+$ - $A^1\Pi(0, 2)$, and $C^1\Sigma^+$ - $A^1\Pi(0, 2)$ spectra, obtained by the VUV- and Vis-FT complementary techniques in the energy regions of the six crossing points ($e$- and $f$-symmetry, $|\Omega| = 0, 1, 2$) between the $a^3\Pi(v = 13)$ and $A^1\Pi(v = 2)$ states, reveal that the perturbation pathways are indirect, primarily facilitated by the $e^3\Sigma^-(v = 4)$ state, and that quantum mechanical interferences via its F1e and F3e components occur.

title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
summary: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine-tune molten-copper and water potentials against experimental diffusion coefficients together with structural constraints. For water, jointly optimizing diffusion and the oxygen-oxygen radial distribution function also improves the predictions of shear viscosity and rotational relaxation, neither of which is included in the optimization objective. Alignment at a single temperature also improves the apparent activation energies of multiple dynamical observables, bringing their temperature dependences closer to experiments. Moreover, the optimized potential exhibits smaller force errors relative to an independent, higher-level quantum-chemical reference, indicating that alignment with experiments improves the fidelity of the potential energy surface beyond the fitted targets. PathGrad thus establishes a general framework for incorporating experimental observables directly into force field optimizations.

title: Fast and Accurate Boys Function Evaluation Using Nonuniform Gridded Taylor Expansions
summary: Efficient Boys function evaluation is important for Gaussian integral calculations on both central processing units (CPUs) and graphics processing units (GPUs). Gridded Taylor expansion provides a simple evaluation procedure, but a uniformly spaced reference table requires substantial storage over a wide argument range. We address this limitation using a nonuniform grid whose spacing increases with the argument. For large arguments, we introduce a normalized auxiliary function whose scaling and derivative properties allow it to be evaluated using the same Taylor procedure as the main-domain Boys functions. The main-domain and large-argument reference tables are constructed jointly, with polynomial degrees and grid parameters selected under accuracy and storage constraints. Low-part corrections to the reference values are included to improve the accuracy of the Taylor evaluation. The resulting method is implemented in the Fast and Accurate BOys (FABO) library and evaluated in QUICK and NWChem-Simint. FABO gives the smallest maximum and mean errors among the tested implementations for all three reported error measures, with the largest sampled error being approximately 1.067 units in the last place (ULPs). In application benchmarks, FABO reduces the Fock-build time relative to the original Boys evaluators in both applications and is competitive with the other tested implementations.

title: Modeling of Chemically Reactive Gas Flows for Multi-Scale Problems
summary: Accurate modeling of chemical reactions plays a key role in the investigation of high-temperature flows. The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method provides highly accurate solutions for such flows. However, its computational cost becomes prohibitive for low Knudsen regimes. Particle-based continuum methods employing the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) or Fokker-Planck approximations have gained increasing attention in recent years, improve computational efficiency in low-Knudsen regimes by modeling relaxation processes rather than binary collisions, while retaining the particle approach that enables straightforward coupling with DSMC. In the last years, different continuum-based models in the open-source particle code PICLas have been extended to simulate gas mixtures with internal energy modes. The present work focuses on modeling of chemically reactive gas mixtures in the Ellipsoidal Statistical BGK model. Model accuracy is assessed for two test cases of a reactive gases confined in a reservoir.

title: Variance and Higher-Order Moments in Computational Fluctuating Hydrodynamics with Multiplicative Noise
summary: Fluctuating hydrodynamics (FHD) models mesoscopic fluid systems by augmenting classical conservation laws with stochastic flux terms governed by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. While traditional validation of computational FHD (CFHD) algorithms focuses primarily on second-order central moments of equilibrium fluctuations, accurately resolving higher-order moments, such as skewness and kurtosis, is essential for evaluating non-linear functions of hydrodynamic fields. In this work, we analyze finite-volume CFHD discretizations to evaluate second-, third-, and fourth-order central moments of thermodynamic fluctuations. Using the one-dimensional stochastic heat equation, we demonstrate that incorporating multiplicative noise is necessary to recover the expected gamma distribution for temperature in the canonical ensemble, whereas additive noise models yield a Gaussian distribution that fails to capture non-zero skewness and excess kurtosis. We also derive analytical expressions for inherent modeling errors that persist in the limit of vanishing time step for a variety of boundary conditions. Furthermore, we introduce an improved formulation for Dirichlet boundary conditions that eliminates large boundary-adjacent errors in the third central moment present in traditional boundary treatments. We also examine higher-order temporal integration schemes, demonstrating that Stratonovich-based integrators, such as Heun's predictor-corrector method, can reduce these modeling errors. Finally, numerical simulations of the full compressible, stochastic Navier--Stokes equations confirm the generality and practical applicability of the findings obtained from the stochastic heat equation.

title: Efficient spin-lattice dynamics and spin thermometry with machine-learned magnetic potentials
summary: In finite-temperature spin-lattice dynamics, conventional force-only spin thermometers fail for energies nonlinear in each spin, while the standard semi-implicit SIB integrator requires two model evaluations per step. Here we introduce a geometric-probe spin temperature that is exact for arbitrary high-order smooth Hamiltonians using first-order spin forces alone without Hessians, making it naturally suited for nonlinear many-body machine-learning (ML) magnetic potentials. Complementarily, our cached-field integrator (CFI) stays second-order accurate with a single model evaluation per step, about halving the time per step with ML potentials. Extensive benchmarks against Monte Carlo across analytic and ML systems confirm both exact thermometry and accurate thermodynamics.
